note: Organizing Thought (OT) canonical ideas. Phase 2 of Stage 1 — Experience Compass. Each idea is a stable unit of the OT instructional model, structured to be compatible with the instructional_objects.json conventions. OT helps a student ORGANIZE THINKING before the existing Writing workflow. Compass analyzes evidence and offers hypotheses; it never performs the student's cognitive work.

ideas.canonical_statement: An assignment includes a topic and an intellectual task.
ideas.purpose: Help the student separate WHAT the assignment is about from WHAT they are being asked to do with it.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student names a topic but not the intellectual task (explain, argue, compare, interpret, etc.), or vice versa.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Identify both the topic and the intellectual task the assignment requires.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student can state the topic and the task in their own words.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once topic and task are both present — do not require exhaustive analysis.

ideas.canonical_statement: An assignment may contain multiple required tasks.
ideas.purpose: Help the student notice when more than one thing is being asked.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student treats a multi-part assignment as a single task and overlooks required parts.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Identify each required part of the assignment.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student has surfaced the parts that materially affect an adequate response.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the required parts are represented well enough to proceed.

ideas.canonical_statement: Required tasks may relate to one another.
ideas.purpose: Help the student see how the parts connect rather than treating them as a checklist.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student lists parts but does not see how they depend on or serve one another.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Describe how the required parts relate.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student can state at least the principal relationship among the parts.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the relationships needed to plan a response are clear enough.

ideas.canonical_statement: Constraints affect what counts as an adequate response.
ideas.purpose: Help the student attend to audience, evidence, sources, format, length, scope, or perspective.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student ignores constraints that change what an adequate response must include.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Identify the constraints that shape an adequate response.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student has noted the constraints that materially affect the work.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the student has a sufficient working representation of the assignment.

ideas.canonical_statement: The student already knows some relevant things.
ideas.purpose: Help the student recognize their existing knowledge as a starting point.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student assumes they know nothing, or does not distinguish what they already know.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Name what they already understand that is relevant.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student can identify relevant prior knowledge.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once prior knowledge has been surfaced enough to locate real questions.

ideas.canonical_statement: Some relevant things still need to be learned or clarified.
ideas.purpose: Help the student locate genuine gaps that questions can address.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student cannot distinguish what they know from what they still need to find out.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Formulate the questions that must be answered to complete the assignment.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The questions target real gaps relevant to the assignment.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the questions cover the gaps that matter for this assignment.

ideas.canonical_statement: Not every possible question is needed for this assignment.
ideas.purpose: Help the student select assignment-relevant questions rather than generating an exhaustive list.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student lengthens the list with questions that do not serve the assignment.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Select the questions that actually serve this assignment.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The set is manageable and assignment-relevant.
ideas.stopping_rule: Do not reward unnecessary question generation; stop when the set is manageable.

ideas.canonical_statement: The selected questions guide further learning.
ideas.purpose: Help the student see questions as a guide for inquiry, not a formality.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student treats questions as decoration rather than as a guide to what to investigate.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Recognize how the questions will direct their inquiry.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student has a manageable set of questions that can guide productive inquiry.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the questions can guide productive inquiry.

ideas.canonical_statement: Read, observe, or investigate to answer a question.
ideas.purpose: Help the student direct inquiry at their questions.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student gathers material with no question in view.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Investigate in order to answer an identified question.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student's inquiry is aimed at their questions.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once inquiry is oriented to real questions.

ideas.canonical_statement: Information becomes useful when it contributes to answering a question.
ideas.purpose: Help the student judge relevance by usefulness to a question.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student collects information without relating it to any question.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Relate information to the question it helps answer.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: Information is connected to the questions it serves.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the student relates material to their questions.

ideas.canonical_statement: New information should be related to existing understanding.
ideas.purpose: Help the student integrate rather than accumulate.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student holds new information as disconnected facts.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Relate new information to what they already understand.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: New information is integrated with prior understanding.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once integration has begun productively.

ideas.canonical_statement: An idea is not merely copied information.
ideas.purpose: Help the student distinguish constructed ideas from copied wording or collected facts.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student offers copied wording or disconnected facts in place of ideas.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Construct an idea by relating information to a question and to prior understanding.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student's ideas are their own construction, not copied information.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once genuine ideas (not copied information) are present.

ideas.canonical_statement: Useful ideas help answer one or more identified questions.
ideas.purpose: Help the student keep ideas tied to the questions that matter.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student's ideas drift away from the assignment's questions.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Tie each idea to the question(s) it helps answer.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student has enough relevant ideas to begin a Current Answer.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once there are enough relevant ideas to begin constructing a Current Answer.

ideas.canonical_statement: A student can have a provisional answer before everything is known.
ideas.purpose: Help the student commit to a working answer without waiting for certainty.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student refuses to answer until everything is settled.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: State a provisional best answer to the assignment.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student offers a provisional answer.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once a provisional answer exists.

ideas.canonical_statement: Ideas support and shape the Current Answer.
ideas.purpose: Help the student build the answer from their own ideas.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student's answer is not connected to their ideas.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Synthesize their ideas into their best current answer.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The answer is grounded in the student's ideas.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the answer draws on the student's ideas.

ideas.canonical_statement: New ideas may strengthen, qualify, complicate, or change the answer.
ideas.purpose: Help the student treat the answer as responsive to their thinking.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student treats the first answer as fixed regardless of their ideas.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Let ideas revise the answer as needed.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student can adjust the answer in light of their ideas.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the answer reflects the student's current thinking.

ideas.canonical_statement: The Current Answer provides an intellectual center for communication.
ideas.purpose: Help the student see the answer as the center the writing will communicate. It is not automatically a thesis sentence, introduction, or polished draft.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student mistakes the Current Answer for a finished thesis or polished draft.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Hold the answer as the intellectual center for planning communication.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student has a sufficiently coherent Current Answer to begin planning.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the Current Answer is coherent enough to begin planning communication.

ideas.canonical_statement: Communication should help the reader understand the Current Answer.
ideas.purpose: Help the student plan for reader understanding, not for form.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student plans around format rather than reader understanding.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Plan so a reader can understand the Current Answer.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The plan is oriented to reader understanding.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the plan serves reader understanding.

ideas.canonical_statement: Ideas perform communicative jobs.
ideas.purpose: Help the student see each idea as doing a job (introduce, explain, compare, define, present evidence, interpret evidence, address an objection, show consequences, conclude).
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student lists ideas without knowing what job each performs for the reader.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Identify the communicative job each idea performs.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student can name what each part is doing for the reader.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the jobs are clear enough to order them.

ideas.canonical_statement: Order should serve reader understanding.
ideas.purpose: Help the student order parts so the reader can follow.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student orders parts arbitrarily or by template.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Order the parts so a reader can follow the answer.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The order helps a reader understand.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the order serves understanding.

ideas.canonical_statement: A plan is revisable.
ideas.purpose: Help the student hold the plan lightly.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student treats the plan as a rigid contract.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Treat the plan as revisable.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The student understands the plan can change.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the plan is workable and revisable.

ideas.canonical_statement: Planning should not automatically impose a rigid introduction-body-conclusion template.
ideas.purpose: Help the student plan from communicative jobs, not a fixed template.
ideas.blocking_difficulty: The student defaults to a rigid five-paragraph template regardless of the answer.
ideas.required_cognitive_act: Plan from the communicative jobs the answer requires.
ideas.sufficiency_criterion: The plan follows the answer's needs, not a fixed template.
ideas.stopping_rule: Stop once the student can begin writing confidently from the plan.
